instruction.text: Look at the expressions in the following sentences. What do they mean? Select the correct answer.

atoms.a: That quiz was a piece of cake.
b: The quiz tasted like a piece of cake.

atoms.a: He hit the nail on the head when he suggested that our community should do much more for the environment, such as saving more energy.
b: ++ He was right about the need for more climate action.
He hammered some nails into a box.
He talked about climate change while hitting nails on the head.

atoms.a: Ever since I forgot my best friend’s birthday, they’ve been giving me the cold shoulder.
b: ++ My best friend has been ignoring me ever since I forget their birthday.
My best friend wanted me to bring cold ice cream for their birthday.
Ever since my best friend’s birthday, everything has been great.

atoms.a: An apple a day keeps the doctor away.
b: Eating apples makes it hard for your doctor to find you.
Eating fruit is bad for your health.

instruction.text: Select a saying that matches the given meaning.

atoms.a: Don’t wait to do something if you can do it right away.
atoms.b: “Never put off until tomorrow what you can do today.”

atoms.a: Visual representations can give us more information than a plain text.
atoms.b: “A picture is worth a thousand words.”

atoms.a: Defeat is normal. If you keep on trying, you’ll eventually succeed.
Respect those from whom you are receiving something important.
atoms.b: “don’t bite the hand that feeds you.”
